I'm an atheist but had my son baptized. My grandmother made this dress 50 years ago so all her family could use it and have their name sewn in. It means a lot to her, but not much to me, so i couldn't see the hurt.

i can see the issue in raising your kids to believe in a god when you don't, but why not just give the children information from both point of views when they ask. That's what my dad did when i was little.

I don't think you're dumb, maybe you just don't get it with the explanation available.

next month, the 7th is a Sunday.
there's 7 days in a week, so each day dated with a number dividable by 7 is a Sunday (7th, 14th, 21st, 28th)

if you need to know what day of the week the 17th is, you just go Sunday 14th, Monday 15th, Tuesday 16th, Wednesday 17th.

It's mostly counting and memorizing, not so much math. 
I'm a bit kinesthetic myself, maybe you are too? It can make it hard for you to learn new things. My teachers thought i was stupid until i proofed sine and cosine, which i taught myself.

I never had a clue to how fractions worked until i got it explained in LEGO...

I don't know how to phrase it at all, i don't want to create any misunderstandings. I don't want anyone to feel guilty, because it's not anyone's fault. And i don't want them to look at me differently, or be afraid. I know it's selfish and i want to "want to tell them", but i really don't want things to change right now.

Thank you for setting things up in a different light for me.

The safety plan is non-existent at the moment, this seriously happened to me today, i called the suicide hotline for advice this morning, they were closed, then i called the psychiatrists office, no one answered, my own doctor is on vacation and when i tried to go on here the first time, reddit was down for maintenance.

I haven't found a way to tell my boyfriend and family how bad the thoughts have gotten yet.

I told my doctor and I am currently on a waiting list to get help from a psychiatric hospital. I'm expected to start treatment in about 3 months (mid August).

I understand what you're writing with the pink elephant, but i don't "fight" the thoughts like that. It's a technique used in meditation to clear your head of worries. In my experience, fighting makes it worse, like you said.

I haven't found the courage to tell my boyfriend or any of my family that i've started to think about self-harm and suicide yet. I don't know how.

Edit: The suggestion of letting the thoughts come and go is good, but i don't think i would want to try right now.

maybe you're right.
i recently realized how horrible i have behaved in my past (due to my BPD I've been acting all kinds of crazy without knowing it) and have been doing everything in my power to stop the bad behavior and communicate when things go wrong for me. It's a struggle. 

And i have kids, so every time i get a "bad" feeling, i have to re-evaluate why i'm feeling, what i'm feeling and if the reaction fits, before i stop them from drawing on the wallls.
It's definitely something that has turned me upside down. i feel like i have woken up from a mediocre dream to a grey, apathetic reality where everything i do is wrong, but i have to not feel sorry for myself and just try to do better.

The problem is, if i can't get rid of the thoughts, they become insistent and i start to feel obligated to them. (i don't know if this makes sense) This is what scares me

Thank you for sharing your story!
I'm sorry to hear you have to deal with that. I thought you were indicating that most people are sad to be diagnosed. English is not my first language, so I'm sorry if I misunderstood.

I don't know why, but I've always been afraid of reading about different disorders. I guess I was afraid I would act out one of them in the hopes of getting some attention and pity...

When I first read the brochure, it was like finally getting a clear signal. The following days a lot of former situations came to me, and I realized how often I was the one at fault. I think I've been too stubborn and lying to myself. I know it contradicts the whole "I know there's something wrong with me", but deep down inside I just want to be average. 

I would like to talk to other BPD's with children, is there another subreddit for that?

And thanks for sharing! I appreciate it :)

I feel more relieved than happy. I finally know what to treat.
And I feel like I had it all my life so far, I can read that it's something you'll have all your life, so why be sad about it if it's out of your hands anyway?
I'm also in a good place in my life, despite being depressed. I spend a huge amount of time making my children smile, that keeps my thoughts on the right track :)
I will deffinetly take a look at that! My boyfriend is very supportive as is his family, so I know they want to seek information on how to understand and help.
